subject.title: fix(compaction): skip no-op compaction when there is nothing to summarize

question: Should a default empty keep-all compaction be represented as a skipped operation with no compaction entry, while registered `session_before_compact` handlers still receive the preparation?
rationale: This is a deliberate session-history and extension-observability contract change; source-level tests can verify either behavior but cannot choose the product contract.

options.title: Adopt skipped empty compaction
options.body: Rebase and merge the guard so default no-op compactions make no provider request and append no session entry, while handlers retain control of empty preparations.

options.title: Retain compaction entries
options.body: Keep the existing entry/event behavior and pursue a narrower optimization only if it can avoid the request without changing session history semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt skipped empty compaction
recommendation.body: Rebase and merge the guard so default no-op compactions make no provider request and append no session entry, while handlers retain control of empty preparations.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related safeguard-loop report provides the strongest available context for why empty-preparation handling must remain extension-aware, though current-main code ownership could not be established from the available record.
